test_demo_101.subject: Computer Science
test_demo_101.description: Comprehensive evaluation covering stack/queue operations, circular queues, binary tree traversals, and time complexities.
test_demo_101.instructions: Please ensure a stable internet connection. Each question has an individual timer. Once time expires, the answer is locked and auto-advanced.

questions.question: What is the primary time complexity of push and pop operations in a Stack?
questions.explanation: Stack operates on LIFO principle, accessing top element directly in O(1) constant time.

questions.question: True or False: In a Queue, elements are inserted at the front and deleted from the rear.
questions.explanation: In a Queue, elements are ENQUEUED at the rear and DEQUEUED from the front (FIFO).

questions.question: Which tree traversal visits the root node BEFORE its child subtrees?
questions.explanation: Pre-order visits (Root -> Left -> Right). In-order visits (Left -> Root -> Right). Post-order visits (Left -> Right -> Root).

questions.question: A queue condition where rear reaches maximum size while front > 0 is fixed by using a _____ queue.
questions.explanation: Circular queues reuse dequeued spaces by wrapping pointers modulo array length.

questions.question: Explain why binary search tree lookup degrades to O(n) worst-case time complexity.
questions.correctAnswer: When the tree becomes completely unbalanced/skewed, behaving like a linked list.
questions.explanation: If elements are inserted in sorted order, the BST becomes a single chain of height n.
